title: FREDIngester key includes release_date=now() so reruns create duplicates
description: src/data/fred.py:FREDIngester.transform sets 'release_date': pd.Timestamp.utcnow() on every run. _key_columns = ['observation_date', 'release_date', 'series_id']. Result: rerunning the ingester creates a fresh release_date that doesn't match prior rows, the upsert key check passes, and a new row is inserted for every (observation_date, series_id) on every run. Repro: run FREDIngester twice — observation count doubles. The DataProvider already works around this with DISTINCT ON (observation_date, series_id) ORDER BY release_date DESC, but other consumers (like the CL-1sa backtest script) hit duplicate-index errors. Fix options: (1) drop release_date from the key — observation_date+series_id only — and update on conflict; (2) keep release_date but pass it from the FRED API's actual release timestamp (not utcnow); (3) make _upsert_dataframe handle conflicts on (observation_date, series_id) ignoring release_date.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running FREDIngester does not create duplicate observations; DataProvider/backtest queries don't need DISTINCT ON workaround
close_reason:
Changed FREDIngester._key_columns from ['observation_date', 'release_date', 'series_id'] to ['observation_date', 'series_id']. The BaseIngester._upsert_dataframe uses _key_columns to dedup against existing rows BEFORE insert; with release_date in the key, every rerun's fresh utcnow() value made all rows look 'new' and inserted duplicates. Dropping release_date from the dedup key makes (observation_date, series_id) the natural identity, which matches what every consumer treats as canonical anyway. release_date is still written to the row (intended as ALFRED-vintage metadata; not used by current consumers but preserved for future use).

Verified end-to-end: re-ran FREDIngester on IRLTLT01DEM156N (known to have 2 duplicates from yesterday's mishap), wrote 0 new rows, count unchanged at 137. Pre-fix this rerun would have written 137 fresh duplicate rows.

Out of scope: schema migration to drop release_date from macro_data's PRIMARY KEY (currently (observation_date, release_date, series_id)). The 2 existing dup rows from yesterday remain, but DataProvider's DISTINCT ON handles them. A schema migration to clean up + tighten the PK is a separate ticket if needed; the current fix prevents new dups from accumulating.

title: DataProvider.get_aligned_series doesn't merge prices + macro_data — symbols in only one table get dropped
description: src/data/provider.py:get_aligned_series queries prices first; if any symbol is found there, returns immediately without consulting macro_data. Result: queries like get_aligned_series(['EURUSD', 'US_10Y', 'DE_10Y']) return only EURUSD + US_10Y because DE_10Y lives only in macro_data (FRED IRLTLT01DEM156N) and the prices-table lookup non-empty short-circuits the fallback. Repro: seed FRED + yfinance, call get_aligned_series(['EURUSD', 'US_10Y', 'DE_10Y'], 2020-01-01, 2024-01-01), inspect df.columns — only ['EURUSD', 'US_10Y'] present. Impact: rate-diff backtest can't get the DE_10Y leg via the provider; CL-1sa works around by querying macro_data directly. Fix: query both tables, union the results, pivot-merge by ts. Or: per-symbol routing — try prices for each symbol individually, fall back to macro_data for the unfound ones.
acceptance_criteria: get_aligned_series(['EURUSD', 'US_10Y', 'DE_10Y']) returns 3 columns; integration test asserts symbols spread across prices + macro_data both come through
close_reason:
Rewrote DataProvider.get_aligned_series in src/data/provider.py to query both prices and macro_data and merge per-symbol results, instead of short-circuiting on the first non-empty prices result. Logic: (1) query prices for all requested symbols → collect any returned columns; (2) compute set of symbols not yet found AND mappable to FRED; (3) query macro_data with DISTINCT ON for those; (4) concat all per-symbol Series with outer-join on the union of indices; (5) return None only if NO data found for any symbol.

Verified with the original CL-5rtm repro: get_aligned_series(['EURUSD', 'US_10Y', 'DE_10Y'], 2020-01-01, 2024-01-01) now returns shape (1057, 3) with all 3 columns populated (was (1044, 2) pre-fix — DE_10Y silently dropped). EURUSD/US_10Y come from prices (yfinance daily), DE_10Y from macro_data (FRED IRLTLT01DEM156N monthly via outer-join into the daily union — caller can ffill if continuous).

Tests: 4 new integration tests in tests/integration/test_data_provider.py covering: cross-table query returns all columns; prices-only path unchanged; unknown symbols return None; partial-match returns only found columns. Skipped if Postgres unreachable. All passing.

CL-1sa's existing DISTINCT ON workaround in scripts/backtest_rate_diff_mr.py (queries macro_data directly) is no longer required after this fix, but kept for defense in depth — works either way.

title: soak_dashboard.py creates a new SQLAlchemy engine on every /api/soak poll — connection pool leak
description: scripts/soak_dashboard.py:_db_counts creates a fresh create_engine() on every request. With dashboard auto-refreshing every 10s and pool_size=5 default, connections accumulate until Postgres rejects with 'too many clients already' (default max_connections=100). Repro: open the dashboard in a browser tab, leave for ~30 min, then try to connect to postgres elsewhere — fails. Fix: lift create_engine to module scope (lazy singleton) and reuse across requests; OR pass NullPool to opt out of pooling. The dashboard is read-only and low-frequency; either approach works. Caught while seeding historical data — the seed script couldn't even open one connection because the dashboard's pool had exhausted the limit.
acceptance_criteria: dashboard polls for 1h, postgres connection count stays under 20; seed_historical_data.py can connect concurrently
close_reason: Lifted SQLAlchemy engine creation out of the per-request _db_counts() into a module-level lazy singleton _get_engine() in scripts/soak_dashboard.py. Engine is created once on first poll and reused for every subsequent /api/soak request. Pool sized to 2 (read-only, low-frequency dashboard) with max_overflow=0 and pool_pre_ping=True to handle stale connections. Smoke-tested 30 consecutive polls: engine identity unchanged, Postgres pg_stat_activity shows 2 connections (matches pool size, no leak). Previously each poll spun up a new pool of 5+10 default, accumulating connections until Postgres hit max_connections=100 and rejected with 'too many clients already' (which is what blocked the seed_historical_data.py run yesterday).

title: Kelly sizing asserts on garbage inputs — adopt reference's permissive contract
description: src/risk/sizing.py:74-76 has 'assert 0 <= edge <= 1' and 'assert odds >= 0', which crashes on noisy or out-of-range inputs that would naturally arise from upstream estimators. The reference (reference/11_risk_management.md) clamps to [0,1] gracefully without asserts: 'return max(0, min(f, 1))'. The failing test test_kelly_never_negative_regardless_of_input was checking the reference's contract; the current code's strict asserts crashed it. Fix: drop the edge/odds asserts, clamp result to [0, 1] explicitly. Keep the kelly_fraction extension (the one improvement current has over reference). Production rationale: garbage edge from a noisy estimator should yield zero size (no trade), not crash the strategy mid-tick.
acceptance_criteria: test_kelly_never_negative_regardless_of_input passes; test_kelly_bounded_in_unit_interval still passes; test_quarter_kelly_less_than_full_kelly still passes
close_reason: Adopted reference's permissive Kelly contract per recommendation. src/risk/sizing.py:kelly: removed asserts on edge and odds (noisy estimator output should yield zero size, not crash mid-tick). Result clamped to [0, 1] explicitly via max(0, min(1, ...)). Kept the kelly_fraction extension (current code's improvement over reference). kelly_fraction stays asserted because it's a config knob owned by the operator, not a runtime input. test_kelly_never_negative_regardless_of_input passes; test_kelly_bounded_in_unit_interval and test_quarter_kelly_less_than_full_kelly still pass.

title: OIS curve crashes on bootstraps with fewer than 4 points (cubic interp min-count)
description: src/rates/ois_curve.py:97 hardcodes interp1d(kind='cubic') which requires >=4 points. With 1 quote, the discount_factors dict has 2 entries (valuation_date + maturity), and bootstrap raises 'ValueError: The number of derivatives at boundaries does not match: expected 2, got 0+0'. The interpolator never gets set, and any subsequent discount_factor() call raises 'NoneType is not callable'. Reference has the same bug (reference/02 line 350). Failing tests: test_single_quote_curve_roundtrip + test_discount_factors_monotonic_decay. Fix: degree-adaptive interp — n>=4 → cubic, n=3 → quadratic, n=2 → linear. Production curves typically have >5 quotes, so cubic stays the common path; the fix is purely defensive against sparse curves and tests.
acceptance_criteria: test_single_quote_curve_roundtrip passes for all hypothesis examples; test_discount_factors_monotonic_decay passes; existing OIS curve unit tests with full quote sets still pass
close_reason: src/rates/ois_curve.py — two related fixes: (1) _bootstrap now uses degree-adaptive interp1d kind: cubic for n>=4 (production curves), quadratic for n=3, linear for n=2. Asserts n>=2 (need at least one quote). (2) Money-market cutoff in _solve_df_for_quote raised from <=365 to <730 to cover OIS convention (annual coupons start at 2Y, not 1Y) plus calendar-adjustment slack — a 365D quote can bump to ~368 days via NY holiday MFL, and was incorrectly going to multi-coupon branch. (3) discount_factor() now raises ValueError instead of crashing TypeError when called with no interpolator (provides clear diagnostic for sparse-curve gaps). (4) Multi-coupon branch raises ValueError when a needed intermediate DF isn't present. Reference (reference/02) had the same cubic-only bug — did not adopt. Tests test_single_quote_curve_roundtrip + test_discount_factors_monotonic_decay pass; existing OIS tests still pass.

title: Wire SIZE_DOWN_50PCT into PortfolioCoordinator — halve intent target inside blackout window
description: CL-c8th wired BlackoutEvaluator into PreTradeValidator for PAUSE_NEW_ENTRIES + EXIT_FLAT (rejection only — validator's contract is reject-or-accept). SIZE_DOWN_50PCT requires mutating intent.target_position, which belongs at the coordinator (it constructs the final OrderIntent already). Task: (1) PortfolioCoordinator constructor accepts optional blackout_evaluator param; (2) when constructing the 'final' OrderIntent in process_intents, query evaluator and if action == SIZE_DOWN_50PCT halve target_position before passing to PreTradeValidator; (3) emit fx_blackout_size_down_total metric; (4) add coordinator unit test that intents inside SIZE_DOWN_50PCT window get halved before submission. Without this, the engine doesn't size-down ahead of NFP/FOMC and gets full slippage from the entries it's not supposed to be making at full size.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator accepts blackout_evaluator; intents during SIZE_DOWN_50PCT window are halved before validator/OMS; unit test verifies pre-event target=2000 post-coordinator target=1000; fx_blackout_size_down_total metric increments
close_reason:
Wired BlackoutEvaluator into PortfolioCoordinator at the SIZE_DOWN_50PCT layer (CL-c8th's deferred half). Architecture split: validator handles PAUSE_NEW_ENTRIES + EXIT_FLAT (rejection-only — its contract is reject-or-accept, can't mutate); coordinator owns intent construction so it can mutate target_position cleanly for SIZE_DOWN_50PCT.

Changes:
(1) PortfolioCoordinator.__init__ accepts optional blackout_evaluator kwarg (graceful None fallback for unit tests + offline runs).
(2) New _apply_blackout_size_down(symbol, target) helper — runs evaluator with currency=symbol[:3] (matches PreTradeValidator._currency_from_symbol convention), halves target_position when action == SIZE_DOWN_50PCT (sign-preserving so shorts also halve correctly), passes through unchanged for FULL_SIZE / PAUSE / EXIT_FLAT (validator handles the latter two).
(3) Called inline in process_intents BEFORE constructing the final OrderIntent — intent goes to validator already at half size; the journal/OMS see only the post-mutation value.
(4) New metric fx_blackout_size_down_total{pair} — labels per pair, increments on each size-down event. Defined in src/monitoring/metrics.py:blackout_size_down.
(5) run_engine.build_coordinator threads the existing blackout_evaluator (built once at engine boot from configs/economic_calendar.yaml) into the constructor.
(6) 7 new unit tests in test_portfolio_coordinator.py::TestBlackoutSizeDown:
   - SIZE_DOWN window (event 6h away) halves target ✓
   - FULL_SIZE window (event 72h away) leaves target unchanged ✓
   - PAUSE window (45min) coordinator does NOT mutate (validator's job)
   - EXIT_FLAT window (5min) same — coordinator passes through
   - No-evaluator config passes through unchanged
   - USD-only event doesn't size down EUR pair (currency filter)
   - Negative target halved correctly (sign-preserving)

Smoke test: engine builds with both validator.blackout_evaluator AND coordinator.blackout_evaluator true, 7 calendar events loaded. 516 unit tests pass (+7 from this work).

title: Wire economic_calendar BlackoutEvaluator into PreTradeValidator — gate intents around major releases
description: src/data/economic_calendar.py exists with EconomicCalendar / BlackoutEvaluator / BlackoutAction (FULL_SIZE / SIZE_DOWN_50PCT / PAUSE_NEW_ENTRIES / EXIT_FLAT) and 24 unit tests, plus configs/economic_calendar.yaml with 7 tier-1 events. NO CALLERS in src/runtime/, src/portfolio/, src/execution/, src/strategies/. Task: (1) load calendar at engine boot via load_calendar_from_yaml; (2) construct BlackoutEvaluator and pass to PreTradeValidator (or coordinator); (3) on every intent, evaluator.evaluate(now, instrument_currency_pair) returns one of 4 actions; (4) if PAUSE_NEW_ENTRIES → pre-trade rejects with reason 'blackout_pause'; if SIZE_DOWN_50PCT → pre-trade halves size; if EXIT_FLAT → coordinator emits flatten intent; if FULL_SIZE → no-op; (5) prometheus counter fx_blackout_actions_total{action=,instrument=}; (6) integration test with synthetic event 30min away verifies SIZE_DOWN_50PCT path. Without this, system holds full size into NFP/FOMC and eats 50bps+ slippage.

JSON protocol: {action: 'get', name: '...'} -> {ok: true, value: '...'} or {action: 'list'} -> {ok: true, names: [...]}. Peer credential check: only same UID can connect (SO_PEERCRED). On SIGTERM: zero credential memory. Exits on decryption failure (wrong passphrase), user retries.

title: Wire OANDA transaction/fill stream -> event-driven fill confirmation
description: Today both the entry and exit fill lifecycles confirm by POLLING broker.get_positions() each ~300s tick and diffing against a captured baseline (CL-hqyj entry + the shipped exit side). That is correct and co-held-pair-safe, but latency-bound to the strategy tick and blind to per-order fill attribution. OANDA exposes a transaction stream (v3 /accounts/{id}/transactions/stream) carrying ORDER_FILL events with orderID, units, price, tradeID — the OMS currently only journals ORDER_PLACED and never consumes fills (see oms.py comment: 'OANDA fills arrive async via stream and would need a separate fill-stream callback to emit ORDER_FILLED').
design:
SCOPE: add an async consumer of the OANDA transactions stream that emits real ORDER_FILLED events into the OMS journal and (optionally) drives book confirmation directly, replacing/augmenting the poll-and-diff.
BENEFITS: (1) event-driven confirmation — entries/exits confirm in ms not up to 300s, shrinking the reconciliation window further; (2) real per-order fill attribution via orderID/clientOrderID (client_order_id is already set as curlit-<idea_id> on Alpaca; wire the equivalent on OANDA orders) so co-held pairs need no delta inference; (3) accurate ORDER_FILLED journal + fill price/slippage capture; (4) clears the non-terminal PENDING _pending entries (CL-hqyj / review #2 P2) that a FOK path can otherwise leave sticky.
DESIGN NOTES: async task alongside the price stream in live_engine (httpx.AsyncClient, follow the existing stream_prices pattern); reconnect/backoff; idempotent by transaction id; feed EventBook.confirm_entries/confirm_exits by order/trade id instead of position-snapshot delta (keep the poll path as a backstop for missed events — belt and suspenders). title: Truth-study first readout: distributions, reversal, duplicate audit

acceptance_criteria:
1. SAMPLE: enough relevant measured posts for above-noise reads (rough floor: >=30 relevant posts with non-NULL 30-min windows).
2. DISTRIBUTIONS: read p10/p90 + hit rate per topic BEFORE any mean; flag topics where the mean and median disagree in sign (spike-and-reverse shape).
3. REVERSAL: overall + per-topic reversal rate (5m move mostly gone by 60m) — if most reaction dies inside 30 min, note that any actionable use would be latency-bound (out of scope by design).
4. DUPLICATE AUDIT: count near-duplicate/retruth pairs (same or near-same text, different post_id, posted within ~24h — SQL: group by text where text<>''). If material (>~10% of relevant posts or visibly distorting a topic cell), add TEXT-HASH DEDUP AT ANALYSIS TIME in truth_report.py (raw archive stays intact; ingestion untouched).
5. DRIFT: --sample 15 spot-check; if labels look off, re-run classifier at a bumped classifier_version and diff against v1-haiku.
6. VERDICT: write findings to this bead; decide dedup yes/no and whether the study continues, changes instruments, or concludes with 'reaction is faster than any retail loop — no durable edge' (a valid, publishable-internally result).

title: Intraday momentum agent: 4H bias + 5-min entries (PDF strategy) — PARKED behind paper-sample review
description:
Operator-approved design, deliberately deferred. Strategy (from Trading_Indicators_Quick_Reference.pdf): 4H bias via EMA9/21 stack + VWAP side + RSI vs 50; 5-min entries on pullback-to-EMA/VWAP with bounce/rejection, volume >=1.5-2x 20-bar avg, RSI turning; stop defined before entry, 1:2 R:R via Alpaca BRACKET orders; ~1% equity risk/trade. Build decisions already made: EQUITY SHARES not options (5-min holds cannot pay option spreads); Alpaca free IEX 5-min bars; FUSION universe = event desk's confirmed tickers (event direction must agree with 4H bias — never fight the thesis); own strategy book + daily loss cap in kill-switch context; paper-only; max 3 concurrent.

DO NOT BUILD until the review gate passes (see acceptance criteria). Sequence: stabilize exit manager -> 1-2 weeks clean data -> review -> then decide.
acceptance_criteria:
Review gate (check ~2026-08-05, all queryable from alpaca_option_orders exit columns + idea_outcomes):
1. SAMPLE: >=25 exit-managed round trips (exit_reason NOT IN (closed_external)) across >=8 trading days and >=15 tickers.
2. EXIT MIX: no single exit_reason >50% of closes (stop_loss dominance = entries/stops wrong; time_stop dominance = theses too slow for options).
3. GRACE VALIDATION: of positions that touched -40% on entry day, compare final exits vs the -60% valve — did the grace period help or hurt net premium?
4. DELAY VALIDATION: avg pnl_pct of >=9:45 entries vs the day-one 9:30 cohort (-42..-73%) — is the 15-min delay measurably better?
5. EXPECTANCY: E = win%*avgWin - loss%*avgLoss on premium; realized avg loss <= ~45% and avg win >= ~70% (the rules encode ~2:1) or a clearly identified fix.
6. CALIBRATION: win rate by confidence bucket (0.45-0.55 / 0.55-0.65 / 0.65+) should be monotonic — flat means confidence is uninformative; fix upstream BEFORE adding a second strategy.
7. OPS CLEAN: zero unmatched positions, zero exit-manager errors, digests uninterrupted.
DECISION: gate passed + edge confirmed -> build the FUSION variant; gate passed but timing is the weak spot (bad MAE before recovery) -> build as a timing overlay for the event desk first; calibration flat -> do not build, fix idea quality.

title: Polymarket-grounded war-gaming: escalation-vs-fade scenario pairs (gated on proven edge)
description:
The one version of multi-scenario war-gaming worth building — narrow and honest,
because the probabilities come from a real market, not an LLM guess.

WHAT
For a high-urgency geo event, emit a SCENARIO PAIR instead of a single call:
  - escalation branch  -> the directional trade (e.g. long crude/defense, puts on exposed semis)
  - containment/fade branch -> fade the spike (this often already exists as the impact agent's fade_candidates)
weighted by REAL probabilities.

THE HARD CONSTRAINT (what makes it honest)
Fire this ONLY for events that have a LIVE Polymarket market, so the branch
probabilities are actual market prices, not fabricated LLM percentages. Most
GDELT/X events have no Polymarket market -> for those, do nothing (a single
directional call beats fake probabilities). This deliberately limits it to the
handful of named, market-priced events (Taiwan invasion, specific chokepoint/
election markets, etc.).

WHY IT'S SMALL
Builds on the Polymarket layer already in the repo (polymarket_signal.py /
poly_market_probs, the Polymarket broker + cross-asset read). Matching an event
to a live Polymarket market + reading its implied probability is most of the
work; the scenario-pair rendering is a digest/idea-shape addition.

GATE (do NOT start until this is true)
Gated behind CL-6axf (outcome tracking) + CL-g8jl (reflective loop) SHOWING the
base niche/adversarial pipeline actually has edge. Adding another idea-generation
layer before we know the existing ones work is more sophistication on an
unvalidated base. Revisit once ~2-3 weeks of finalized outcomes exist and the
reflective review confirms the pipeline is net-positive.

NOT WORTH IT (rejected alternatives, for the record)
- Full 3-branch war-gaming on every event with LLM-assigned probabilities:
  redundant with fade_candidates + the red-team critic's base-rate attacks, 3x
  the per-event LLM cost, and miscalibrated guessed probabilities = theater.

title: Research hypothesis — UAE capital flight to China; assess tradability
description:
Operator hypothesis (2026-04-28): wealthy individuals migrating UAE → China driving an UAE economic downturn. Worth investigating once the research pipeline (CL-h986) is live; the Idea Agent (CL-n0m8) would naturally assess this kind of macro thesis.

Current state of the question:
- Macro premise plausible but unverified. UAE is historically a RECEIVER of capital flight (Russia post-2022, Chinese principals dodging anti-corruption sweeps, sanctions tier). UAE → China reversal would require a specific catalyst making China more attractive — an unusual prior, not impossible.
- No specific evidence in training cutoff data (Jan 2026) confirming a meaningful UAE → China wealth flow at scale.

Tradability concerns:
- Short AED: peg to USD since 1997. Peg-break is tail event with massive implied-vol carry cost.
- Short UAE equities (DFM, ADX, EWT-style ETFs): wealthy capital is mostly real-estate + private, not public companies.
- Long CNH: UAE flows dwarfed by PBoC interventions + US-China trade dynamics.
- UAE sovereign CDS: most direct, retail-illiquid.
- Short UAE-listed property developers (Emaar, Aldar): best public-market proxy if real-estate is the channel.

What would constitute evidence:
- UAE central-bank balance-of-payments data (capital + financial account)
- Dubai Land Department transaction price indices (real-estate is the channel that matters)
- Direct-flight passenger volumes UAE↔China as a migration proxy
- AED FX onshore-vs-offshore basis (peg stress indicator)
- UAE sovereign CDS spreads vs GCC peers

Action: leave open until research pipeline is online; agent system can ingest, evidence-check, and recommend trade construction (or REJECT if evidence absent). If evidence emerges, the Idea Agent → Implementer → Bull/Bear → Verdict flow handles it end-to-end.
acceptance_criteria: Once CL-x561 (research_loop) is live, this hypothesis runs through the pipeline; outcome is PROMOTE (with cited evidence) / REJECT (no detectable signal) / ESCALATE (mixed)
close_reason: Pipeline verdict: REJECT (idea-agent DECLINE, 2026-07-14). Hypothesis injected as operator extract 8dd7e927…f73 and run through research_loop. Rationale: no confirming evidence; all five evidence indicators (UAE BoP, Dubai Land Dept indices, UAE-China flight volumes, AED onshore/offshore basis, UAE CDS vs GCC) outside current ingestion footprint; no trade expression reachable in execution universe (short AED = peg tail-risk w/ carry cost, UAE equities/developers = not FX, CNH = not G10 + dwarfed by PBoC); no falsifiable abandon condition. Full reason in data/research/state.json ideas_processed. Re-open only if evidence emerges AND an ingestible indicator + tradable expression exist.

title: migrations/run.py splits SQL on bare ';' — breaks if a comment contains a semicolon
description: migrations/run.py:41 does sql.split(';') without stripping line comments first.
